speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you describe your fever pattern and what you mean by "altered mentation"? Are you experiencing any other symptoms like a headache, neck stiffness, or recent travel?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of tics and current haloperidol use, I need to rule out a medication side effect; are you experiencing any involuntary muscle movements, stiffness, or difficulty swallowing? I will also check your vital signs for signs of autonomic instability such as high blood pressure or rapid heart rate. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any muscle rigidity, and are you currently sweating profusely or experiencing fluctuating blood pressure? I will also check your creatine kinase levels to assess for muscle breakdown. REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Kinase

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated creatine kinase, leukocytosis, and history of haloperidol use strongly suggest Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. I will now check your core body temperature and assess for the characteristic "lead-pipe" muscle rigidity to confirm this diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Core_Body_Temperature

speaker: Doctor
text: The triad of high fever, severe muscle rigidity, and elevated CK in the context of haloperidol use confirms Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
